recommendedAction.explanation: From-scratch GW1 squad. No transfer action applies until the human manager creates the initial squad in FPL.

pickTeam.explanation: Start a 3-4-3 built around Haaland captaincy, Saka vice-captaincy, Gabriel's Arsenal defensive fixture, João Pedro's Chelsea forward slot, and the highest-projection value midfielders. Lewis-Potter is first outfield bench because he is the best cheap playable attacker outside the XI.

alternatives.upsideCase: Highest selected projection, strong historical minutes, high-confidence first penalty role, and public lineup evidence includes him.
alternatives.downsideCase: Odds report has no matched GW1 market rows, so the captaincy case is not market-checked.

alternatives.upsideCase: Arsenal have the best GW1 fixture in the squad, Saka has high-confidence first penalty role, and RotoWire predicted-lineup evidence includes him.
alternatives.downsideCase: Lower projection than Haaland and Bruno, and public odds coverage is unavailable.

alternatives.upsideCase: Strong forward projection and both FFScout and RotoWire public lineup captures include him.
alternatives.downsideCase: Chelsea penalty role belongs to Palmer in set-piece evidence, so João Pedro lacks the set-piece floor Saka and Haaland have.

alternatives.upsideCase: Man City attacker with high-confidence first direct-free-kick role.
alternatives.downsideCase: Minutes are watch-level and he is clearly behind Haaland for Man City captaincy.

captaincy.explanation: Captain Haaland because he is the top selected projection, has a high-confidence first penalty role, has strong historical minutes, and appears in public predicted-lineup evidence. Vice Saka because Arsenal have Coventry City at home, Saka is first-choice penalty taker in set-piece evidence, and RotoWire includes him in the predicted XI.

reasons: Season strategy says save chips for doubles, blanks, or exceptional captaincy edges.
GW1 is an initial squad-building week, not a chip-attack week.
Odds-report has no matched GW1 market rows, so there is no market-backed chip edge.
This is a from-scratch initial squad, not a transfer plan.
No configured squad exists to sell from.
concerns: Final player choices should still be checked against late public team news before the deadline.

confidence.label: medium
confidence.explanation: Medium confidence because FPL data, fixtures, team-news availability, set-piece roles, historical minutes, and public rendered evidence are fresh. Confidence is capped because Football-Data has no matched GW1 odds rows and predicted-lineup evidence is captured but not yet normalized into player-level confidence.

decisionAnalysis.summary: This draft changes direction from the scrapped GW1 squad by restoring Saka and adding João Pedro while keeping Haaland, Gabriel, Cherki, and a playable bench. Bruno Fernandes is the major omission: he is a stronger pure projection than Saka, but Saka plus João Pedro costs £1.0m less than Bruno plus Calvert-Lewin, avoids triple Leeds exposure, keeps Arsenal's Coventry City home fixture, and leaves £1.0m bank.
squadStructure: Premium spine: Haaland, Saka, Gabriel, and João Pedro give captaincy, Arsenal fixture access, elite defensive projection, and a strong second forward.
Budget discipline: the squad uses £99.0m, leaving £1.0m bank for late price or team-news pivots.
Formation: 3-4-3 starts the highest-evidence forward trio and keeps Lewis-Potter as first outfield bench.
Club exposure: Arsenal, Man City, Leeds, Everton, Brentford, and Spurs are all at two or fewer players, so no club is maxed.

whyPicked: Kelleher is projected third among goalkeepers at £5.0m and has 3330 historical minutes.
FFScout public predicted-lineup capture includes Kelleher for Brentford, so he is not just a historical-minutes pick.

comparedAgainst.name: Raya
whyNot: Raya has the best goalkeeper projection and Arsenal fixture, but costs £1.0m more and would squeeze the Saka-Gabriel-Haaland-João Pedro structure.

whyPicked: Dubravka is the cheapest selected goalkeeper at £4.0m and has 3150 historical minutes.
The second goalkeeper slot should not take budget from the XI while the first goalkeeper is playable.

comparedAgainst.name: Verbruggen
whyNot: Verbruggen has strong minutes at £4.5m, but the extra £0.5m is less useful than preserving the £1.0m bank.

whyPicked: Gabriel is the top projected defender at 5.8 and Arsenal open at home to Coventry City.
Both FFScout and RotoWire public lineup captures include Gabriel, and he has 2750 historical minutes.

comparedAgainst.name: Nico O'Reilly
whyNot: O'Reilly is cheaper and has Man City exposure, but Gabriel's projection, fixture, and public lineup support are stronger for GW1.

whyPicked: Keane is a £5.0m defender with 2588 historical minutes and a strong 3.9 projection.
Everton have the best six-week average fixture difficulty in the ticker, which supports using a value Everton defender.

comparedAgainst.name: Tarkowski
whyNot: Tarkowski is a stronger Everton defender on total points, but costs £1.0m more and does not improve the squad enough to justify losing bank or an attacker.

whyPicked: Digne is the highest projected available defender at £4.5m in the budget defender pool.
He keeps the defence cheap enough to afford Saka and João Pedro while still offering set-piece-adjacent upside from corner/indirect role evidence.

comparedAgainst.name: Tyrick Mitchell
whyNot: Mitchell has stronger historical minutes, but Digne has the better generated projection and more attacking-route evidence.

whyPicked: Sessegnon is a playable £4.5m bench defender with 1816 historical minutes.
He is kept on the bench because Fulham's Chelsea opener is difficult, but his price protects the squad structure.

comparedAgainst.name: Calvin Bassey
whyNot: Bassey has more minutes, but Sessegnon has the better generated projection and is acceptable as second outfield bench.

whyPicked: Spence is a £4.5m bench defender with 2049 historical minutes.
He avoids using a dead £4.0m defender, which matters because the squad is meant to remain playable through early uncertainty.

comparedAgainst.name: Alex Murphy
whyNot: Murphy is £0.5m cheaper, but has only 7 historical minutes and would make the bench fragile.

whyPicked: Saka restores Arsenal attacking exposure for Coventry City at home and set-pieces-report lists him as Arsenal's high-confidence first penalty taker.
RotoWire public lineup evidence includes Saka, and he is the vice-captain because his fixture and penalty role give a clear fallback captaincy route.

comparedAgainst.name: Bruno Fernandes
whyNot: Bruno projects higher and has penalties, but Saka plus João Pedro costs £1.0m less than Bruno plus Calvert-Lewin while keeping Arsenal's best GW1 attacking fixture.

whyPicked: Cherki is a £7.5m Man City attacker with a 5.1 projection and a high-confidence first direct-free-kick role.
He adds Man City attacking exposure alongside Haaland without needing the £8.5m Semenyo spend.

comparedAgainst.name: Semenyo
whyNot: Semenyo has stronger historical minutes and total points, but costs £1.0m more and does not beat Cherki's projection or direct-free-kick role.

whyPicked: Wilson is a £6.5m midfielder with a 4.8 projection and 2674 historical minutes.
RotoWire public lineup evidence includes Harry Wilson, making him a stronger current pick than a pure projection artifact.

comparedAgainst.name: Bruno Guimarães
whyNot: Bruno Guimarães has the same projection, but Newcastle open against Liverpool and Wilson has a better immediate public-lineup/fixture blend.

whyPicked: Okafor is a £6.0m midfielder with a 4.7 projection, which is strong for the price.
He keeps the midfield affordable enough to carry Saka, Cherki, Haaland, João Pedro, and Gabriel together.

comparedAgainst.name: Gibbs-White
whyNot: Gibbs-White has more secure minutes and a strong role, but costs £2.0m more and would force a major downgrade elsewhere.

whyPicked: Lewis-Potter is first outfield bench because he is the best projected sub-£5.6m midfielder and has 1960 historical minutes.
His high-confidence direct-free-kick role gives him more emergency upside than a defensive bench-only slot.

comparedAgainst.name: Aaronson
whyNot: Aaronson is close on price and minutes, but Lewis-Potter has the better generated projection and set-piece route.

whyPicked: Haaland is the highest selected projection and set-pieces-report lists him as Man City's high-confidence first penalty taker.
Public predicted-lineup evidence includes him, and his captaincy profile is clearer than spreading funds into a no-Haaland build.

comparedAgainst.name: No-Haaland balanced structure
whyNot: A no-Haaland structure improves budget spread, but removes the cleanest captaincy option and increases reliance on weaker captain alternatives.

whyPicked: João Pedro is the second-highest forward projection after Haaland and has 2658 historical minutes.
Both FFScout and RotoWire public lineup captures include him, which supports starting him despite Chelsea's penalty hierarchy favoring Palmer.

comparedAgainst.name: Watkins
whyNot: Watkins is reliable and has strong minutes, but João Pedro projects higher and is £0.5m cheaper.

whyPicked: Beto is the best-projected £5.5m forward in the evidence pack and helps fund the premium core.
FFScout public lineup evidence includes Beto, reducing the risk that the pick is purely historical.

comparedAgainst.name: Calvert-Lewin
whyNot: Calvert-Lewin has Leeds penalty evidence, but costs £0.5m more and would reduce the bank while projecting lower than Beto.

whyCaptain: Haaland has the highest selected projection and the clearest goal-heavy captaincy profile.
He has high-confidence penalty evidence, strong historical minutes, and public predicted-lineup support.

comparedAgainst.name: Saka
whyNot: Saka is vice-captain because Arsenal have Coventry City at home and he has penalties, but Haaland still has the better scoring profile and selected projection.

comparedAgainst.name: João Pedro
whyNot: João Pedro has public lineup support and a strong projection, but lacks first-penalty evidence at Chelsea.

comparedAgainst.name: Cherki
whyNot: Cherki has direct-free-kick upside, but his minutes are less secure than Haaland's and he is behind Haaland for Man City captaincy.

keyOmissions.name: Bruno Fernandes
whyOmitted: Bruno is omitted because the Saka plus João Pedro structure matches the Bruno plus Calvert-Lewin projection, saves £1.0m, avoids triple Leeds exposure, and keeps Arsenal attacking coverage.
wouldReconsiderIf: Man Utd public evidence becomes materially stronger than Arsenal and Chelsea evidence.
Late team news weakens Saka or João Pedro.

keyOmissions.name: Raya
whyOmitted: Raya is omitted because Gabriel and Saka already give double Arsenal exposure, and spending £6.0m on goalkeeper would reduce squad flexibility.
wouldReconsiderIf: A cheaper outfield structure frees £1.0m without losing Saka, Gabriel, Haaland, or João Pedro.

keyOmissions.name: Semenyo
whyOmitted: Semenyo is omitted because Cherki is £1.0m cheaper, has the better projection in the evidence pack, and owns the first direct-free-kick role.
wouldReconsiderIf: Predicted-lineup evidence weakens Cherki or public odds eventually favor Semenyo's attacking role.

risks: Football-Data odds-report has no matched GW1 Premier League market rows, so scoring and clean-sheet assumptions are not market-checked.
Cherki, Okafor, Beto, Digne, Sessegnon, and Lewis-Potter depend on value-role confidence rather than fully normalized predicted-lineup confidence.
Bruno Fernandes is omitted despite being the highest projected midfielder and having first penalties/direct free kicks.
Chelsea penalty evidence favors Palmer, so João Pedro's case is projection and lineup based rather than set-piece based.
The squad relies on Haaland captaincy; a late Man City lineup concern would require a major pivot.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: Any selected player appears as risk or avoid in a refreshed team-news report.
Late public predicted-lineup evidence removes Saka, Gabriel, João Pedro, Haaland, Wilson, Kelleher, Beto, or Cherki from expected XIs.
Matched GW1 odds rows strongly favor Bruno/Man Utd over Saka/Arsenal or João Pedro/Chelsea.
A legal Bruno structure keeps Saka or Gabriel, avoids dead bench players, and preserves at least £0.5m bank.
FPL price, position, or availability changes alter the £99.0m structure before deadline.
